items.title: What does a reconditioned engine cost in the UK?
items.description: The short answer: Reconditioned engines cost between £2,100 and £3,500 supply-only for most 4-cylinder engines. Fitted costs range from £3,500 to £5,500 depending on engine type, vehicle, and location.

blocks.text: The longer answer: For most UK drivers replacing a common 4-cylinder diesel or petrol engine, expect to pay £2,100–£3,500 supply-only for a reconditioned unit with a 12-month warranty. Fitting adds £800–£2,200 depending on your location and the garage you choose.

Why reconditioned is the most popular choice: Based on 24,650 quote requests in 2025, reconditioned engines were chosen in 70.45% of cases [EM-VERIFIED] . For vehicles worth between £4,000 and £15,000, reconditioned was the most common choice, reflecting the ideal balance of cost and warranty.

[EM-QUOTE] These figures are derived from actual supplier quotes submitted through our platform for reconditioned engines. Fitted costs assume independent specialist labour at regional average rates. Main dealer costs are typically 40–60% higher.

items.title: What does "reconditioned" actually mean?
items.description: Understanding what a reconditioned engine actually is — and what it isn't — is critical before you buy one. Unlike a used engine, which is sold "as-is," a reconditioned engine has been professionally dismantled, cleaned, measured, machined, and rebuilt to a defined standard.

blocks.text: This is the standard engineering procedure used by reputable UK engine specialists:
Complete disassembly of block, cylinder head, valvetrain, and crank assembly for inspection.
High-temp ultrasonic wash or shot-blast to eliminate carbon buildup, oil sludge, and corrosion.
Micrometer measurement for bore ovality, journal wear, and ultrasonic crack testing.
Cylinder honing/re-boring, crankshaft journal regrinding, and precision head skimming.
New piston rings, big end & main bearings, thrust washers, seals, and timing chain/belt kit.
Torqued strictly to OEM factory specifications with new gaskets, head bolts, and sealants.
Rigorous compression testing, oil pressure verification, leak-down testing, and live spin test.

items.title: What's covered — and what's not
items.description: The warranty is the biggest reason to choose a reconditioned engine over a used one. Unlike used engines (which are often parts-only), reconditioned engines typically come with a comprehensive warranty covering both parts and labour.

blocks.text: Most common: 12 months parts and labour is the industry benchmark for reconditioned engines from vetted suppliers.

items: Internal engine components: Pistons, rings, bearings, camshaft, crankshaft, connecting rods.
Cylinder head components: Valves, springs, camshafts (if included).
Structural integrity: Block cracks (if discovered early).
Timing components: If replaced as part of the reconditioning build.
Labour: Removal and refitting labour if the unit fails within the warranty period.

blocks.text: ❌ What Warranty Typically Does NOT Cover

cards.title: 🔧 Incorrect installation
cards.text: If the engine is fitted incorrectly or timing setup incorrectly, warranty is void. Always use a qualified garage.
cards.fullText: 🔧 Incorrect installation If the engine is fitted incorrectly or timing setup incorrectly, warranty is void. Always use a qualified garage.

cards.title: ⚠️ Neglect & Overheating
cards.text: Running with no oil, overheating, or ignoring dashboard warning lights voids warranty terms.
cards.fullText: ⚠️ Neglect & Overheating Running with no oil, overheating, or ignoring dashboard warning lights voids warranty terms.

cards.title: 🏁 Racing or Track Use
cards.text: Reconditioned road engines are not warranted for competitive, mapped, or track use.
cards.fullText: 🏁 Racing or Track Use Reconditioned road engines are not warranted for competitive, mapped, or track use.

cards.title: ⚙️ Ancillary Components
cards.text: Alternator, starter, fuel injectors, turbocharger, and pumps are not covered unless explicitly invoiced.
cards.fullText: ⚙️ Ancillary Components Alternator, starter, fuel injectors, turbocharger, and pumps are not covered unless explicitly invoiced.

cards.title: 🔍 Unforeseen Damage
cards.text: If fitting reveals existing issues (faulty wiring loom, split intercooler), these are not covered.
cards.fullText: 🔍 Unforeseen Damage If fitting reveals existing issues (faulty wiring loom, split intercooler), these are not covered.

cards.title: 🔩 General Wear and Tear
cards.text: Normal perishable wear items (external auxiliary belts, hoses, fluids) are excluded.

blocks.text: This is the single biggest financial safeguard of a reconditioned engine over a used engine:

Scenario (Used Engine): You buy a used engine for £1,200 with a 3-month parts-only warranty. After 6 weeks, it develops rod knock. The breaker provides another engine, but you must pay £800–£1,500 garage labour again out of pocket.

Scenario (Reconditioned Engine): You purchase a reconditioned engine for £2,800 with 12 months parts and labour warranty. If it suffers internal failure, the supplier covers both the unit replacement and the garage labour to strip and refit.

items.title: The £600–£1,000 decision
items.description: The price difference between a used engine and a reconditioned engine is typically £600–£1,000 for a standard 4-cylinder unit. Here is what that difference buys you.

blocks.text: ✅ When Reconditioned Is Worth the Premium
Vehicle worth £4,000–£15,000: Warranty protects vehicle capital.
Keeping car 2+ years: Recovers initial outlay over reliable ownership.
Daily essential transport: Cannot tolerate repeat breakdown downtime.
Known flaw engines: Rebuild fixes N47 timing or SDV6 crank weaknesses.
Vehicle worth under £4,000: Recon cost exceeds total car value.
Selling within 12 months: Short ownership won't benefit from long warranty.
Tight upfront budget: Lowest initial cash outlay required.
DIY mechanics: Capable of swapping unit yourself if replacement needed.

The Core Equation: How much is a 12-month parts-and-labour warranty worth to you? • If you value peace of mind → Choose reconditioned. • If lowest upfront price is everything → Choose used (accepting labour risk on failure). Average cost of used engine failure (labour only to swap again): £800–£1,500. A reconditioned unit eliminates this secondary risk.

blocks.question: How much does a reconditioned engine cost in the UK? +
blocks.answer: Reconditioned engines cost £2,100–£3,500 supply-only for most 4-cylinder engines. Fitted costs range from £3,500 to £5,500 . V6 and V8 engines cost significantly more: £3,200–£9,500+ supply-only.

blocks.question: Is a reconditioned engine better than a used engine? +
blocks.answer: Yes, for most applications. A reconditioned engine has been stripped, cleaned, inspected, and rebuilt with new wearing parts. It includes a 12-month parts and labour warranty . A used engine is sold "as-is" with unknown history and minimal warranty.

blocks.question: What's the difference between reconditioned and rebuilt? +
blocks.answer: Reconditioned engines are rebuilt to a defined standard with new wearing parts and full testing. Rebuilt engines vary in quality — some are full custom rebuilds with upgraded components, others are basic localized repairs. Always ask what's included.

blocks.question: What warranty comes with a reconditioned engine? +
blocks.answer: Typically 12 months parts and labour . Some premium suppliers offer 18 or 24 months. Always confirm warranty terms in writing.

blocks.question: Is a reconditioned engine worth the extra cost over used? +
blocks.answer: For most vehicles worth £4,000–£15,000 , yes. The £600–£1,000 premium buys a 12-month parts and labour warranty, new wearing parts, and peace of mind. If your vehicle is worth under £4,000, a used engine may be more cost-effective.

blocks.question: How long does a reconditioned engine last? +
blocks.answer: A properly reconditioned engine should last 80,000–150,000 miles with proper maintenance. The quality of the reconditioning and your maintenance after installation are key factors.

blocks.question: What's included in a reconditioned engine? +
blocks.answer: Typically: new piston rings, bearings, gaskets, seals, timing components (where applicable), and sometimes oil pump and water pump. The engine is fully bench-tested before delivery.

blocks.question: Can I fit a reconditioned engine myself? +
blocks.answer: Only if you are a qualified professional mechanic. Most warranties require professional installation by a registered garage. DIY installation will void the warranty.

blocks.question: How do I know if my vehicle needs a reconditioned engine? +
blocks.answer: If your engine has suffered catastrophic failure (snapped timing belt/chain, spun rod bearings, crankshaft snap, or severe cylinder head warp) and your vehicle is worth over £4,000, a reconditioned engine is usually the best option.

blocks.question: What's the most requested reconditioned engine? +
blocks.answer: The BMW N47D20C is the most requested reconditioned engine, with 1,450 requests in 2025 [EM-VERIFIED] . The Mercedes OM651 is second with 1,250 requests.

blocks.question: What vehicles are reconditioned engines typically bought for? +
blocks.answer: Reconditioned engines are most commonly purchased for vehicles aged 8–15 years , valued at £4,000–£15,000 , where the owner plans to keep the car for 2+ years.

blocks.question: What's the satisfaction rate for reconditioned engines? +
blocks.answer: Based on post-installation surveys, 92% of owners who chose a reconditioned engine reported satisfaction [EM-SURVEY] . The main reasons: reliability, warranty coverage, and peace of mind.

blocks.question: What should I ask before buying a reconditioned engine? +
blocks.answer: Ask: what's included in the reconditioning process? What parts are replaced? What's the warranty and what does it cover? Can you provide a compression test report? Can you send a video of the engine running?

blocks.question: How much does fitting a reconditioned engine cost? +
blocks.answer: Fitting typically costs £800–£2,200 depending on engine type and labour rates. 4-cylinder engines: 6–11 hours. 6-cylinder: 10–14 hours. V8: 14–20+ hours. Regional labour rates vary from £65/hr (North) to £180/hr (London).

blocks.question: Is a reconditioned engine cheaper than a new engine? +
blocks.answer: Yes. A reconditioned engine typically costs 40–70% less than a new OEM crate engine. For a typical 4-cylinder, new costs £4,500–£8,000+ while reconditioned costs £2,100–£3,500.
